meta.name: Limnalis extension corpus (project-authored)
meta.purpose: Project-authored coverage extension closing the vendored corpus blind spots listed in spec section 17.4: logical connectives computed LIVE through sub-expression evaluation (atom-level fixture bindings, not claim-id keying), unparenthesized operator precedence per the recovered EBNF A.9, and the session semantics added in milestone 7 wave 2 (EvaluationSession.shared_state per section 16.6.3 and EvaluationStep.claim_subset per section 16.2.1), including the consolidated spec section 17.2 A11 narrative (test://baseline/by_context_v1, sessions s_shared/s_isolated) that the vendored A11 case does not pin. Cases C1..C4 are the Track C paradox-forensics gallery (liar, Schwarzschild, decoherence cat, Banach-Tarski): four bundles with deterministic live fixtures and pinned expectations, also mirrored as examples/paradox_*.lmn. TRACK LABELING CONSTRAINT: the vendored fixture-corpus schema pins ConformanceCase.track to the enum ["A", "B"], so all extension cases carry track "A" (the closest legal value: they are feature-focused cases in the track-A style) while their ids use the reserved "D" and "C" prefixes (D1..D7, C1..C4) to keep them unambiguously separate from the vendored A1..A14/B1..B2 cases.
phase_order: resolve active frame and evaluator panel
initialize or reuse session baseline service
evaluate adequacy assessments and joint adequacy groups
aggregate claim results under the resolution policy
fold blocks per evaluator, then aggregate block results

ast_decisions.topic: Extension corpus track labeling under the vendored schema

validation.track: vendored schema enum ["A", "B"] — track "D" is not legal, so extension cases use track "A" with id prefix "D"

ast_decisions.notes: The vendored fixture-corpus schema (immutable) constrains ConformanceCase.track to the enum ["A", "B"]. Extension cases are therefore labeled track "A" — they are feature-pinning cases in the track-A style — and are distinguished from vendored cases by the "D" id prefix (D1..D7) and by this corpus file itself.

ast_decisions.topic: IMPLIES/IFF chains are left-associative binary trees
ast_decisions.notes: AND/OR are associative in the spec section 4 pair algebra, so the EBNF repetition maps to one flat n-ary LogicalExprNode (a AND b AND c -> and(a, b, c)). IMPLIES/IFF are NOT associative ((a->b)->c differs from a->(b->c) in section 4), so their chains normalize to LEFT-NESTED BINARY nodes: the EBNF repetitions read left-to-right — `ImplExpr ::= OrExpr { ImplOp OrExpr }` (reconstructed spec A.9 line 1236) and `IffExpr ::= ImplExpr { IffOp ImplExpr }` (line 1235) each extend the expression already read — so a -> b -> c is implies(implies(a, b), c) and t <=> f <=> f is iff(iff(t, f), f). The runtime evaluator folds any residual n-ary implies/iff node (still admitted by the AST model and vendored schema) left-associatively pairwise, matching this reading. Pinned end-to-end by D7; supersedes the flat-n-ary shape briefly emitted mid-milestone-7, whose evaluation silently dropped operands past the second (m7 red-team CRITICAL-1).

ast_decisions.topic: Composed-claim reasons under live sub-expression evaluation
ast_decisions.notes: Live LogicalExpr composition derives reasons per spec section 16.6.6 (m7 red-team HIGH-3 remediation; supersedes the earlier decision that composed results carry no reason, which violated the section 8.5 rule that B and N always require reason codes): when the composed truth is B or N, the sub-results whose truth equals the composed truth determine it — if they carry exactly one distinct reason it is inherited (e.g. D1 c2 t AND b -> B[source_conflict], D1 c3 t AND n -> N[undefined_term], D2 c2 NOT b -> B[source_conflict]); otherwise the reason is logical_composition and the contributing child reasons are recorded in an info diagnostic. T/F composed results still carry no reason (F reasons are optional annotations per section 8.5). The same derivation applies to the per-evaluator block fold (e.g. C4 block local, ev_zf: N AND N -> N[missing_binding]), where the vendored BlockExpectation schema pins truth values only, so block-level reasons are pinned by tests/test_extension_corpus.py instead. Under multi-evaluator paraconsistent_union with NO T/F conflict, a single unique evaluator-local reason IS inherited by the aggregate (e.g. C4 c1 aggregates to T with the zf evaluator's missing_binding reason carried as disclosure).

ast_decisions.topic: License reason vocabulary under live compose_license
ast_decisions.notes: Score-N adequacy now follows the consolidated spec: an assessment whose score is declared N (or whose RESOLVED method computes the non-numeric sentinel "N") yields N[not_yet_applicable] — the first implementation of the spec section 9.2/16.6.4 code — plus a warning-severity diagnostic adequacy_score_not_yet_applicable (C2 aa_core; m7 red-team MEDIUM-1 remediation, superseding the earlier N[missing_binding]+error pin whose cited vendored ast_decision "unresolved_method -> N[missing_binding]" covers only unresolved methods and is preserved: a method with no registered handler and no score still yields N[missing_binding] with the error diagnostic). One divergence from the section 16.6.4 prose REMAINS pinned: an anchor with NO adequacy record for the resolved task licenses N[no_adequacy_result] (C1 l1, C4 c2) — a reason code outside the section 8.5 taxonomy — where the spec sketch assigns N[not_yet_applicable] to the no-record case too.

ast_decisions.topic: Assumption records have no surface-grammar form
ast_decisions.notes: AssumptionNode exists in the AST model and schema, but the normalizer has no assumption-block surface syntax (pre-existing gap, unrelated to the milestone 7 wave 1-2 changes). C4 therefore records the axiom of choice as an ACTIVE placeholder anchor (a_choice) plus a meta-stratum note claim; no runtime code was modified.

ast_decisions.topic: Baseline reference offsets are fixed at 0
ast_decisions.notes: The normalizer accepts only |0:ref| baseline references; the sketched C2 form |inf:finite_time| is not legal surface syntax. C2 c2 pins the declared-unboundedness dynamic as `curvature --> divergence_within_finite_time` (DynamicExpr, op=approaches per the EBNF `-->` spelling) evaluated by a live dynamic-expression handler.

behavior.description: ATOM-LEVEL evaluator binding: keys on predicate NAMES, never on claim ids. Each zero-arity predicate leaf resolves independently, so any LogicalExpr over these atoms is composed by the live spec section 4 Belnap-Dunn pair algebra (implemented in runtime._eval_logical_expr). This removes the vendored atoms_v1 blindness, where truths are keyed on claim ids and composition is never computed.

Context-sensitive baseline criterion per the consolidated spec section 17.2 A11 narrative. Resolves through the wave-2 services["baseline_criterion_resolver"] path under the effective step context (with the baseline-local frame overlay of section 16.2.1 applied), so fixed-mode caching per section 16.6.3 is exercised for real: cache key (session_id, baseline_id) when the session has shared_state=true, and (session_id, step_id, baseline_id) when shared_state=false; on_reference baselines re-resolve at every referencing-claim evaluation.
behavior.unmapped_context: resolution error (baseline_resolution_error diagnostic, baseline left unresolved)

behavior.description: Baseline-comparison evaluator per the spec section 17.2 A11 narrative, in which sensor_A is fixed at 10. Returns T when every BaselineRefTerm in the claim expression resolves to a ready baseline whose materialized value equals the expected sensor value; F otherwise (a missing, non-ready, or non-matching baseline, or a claim with no baseline reference, all yield F).

Liar-forensics evaluator. Predicate leaves resolve by NAME: the predicate "false" resolves N[undefined_term] (the liar sentence is an undefined term for the truth evaluator); unknown predicate names also resolve N[undefined_term]. JudgedExpr claims dispatch on the expression's criterionRef against the live criterion pack (see test://paradox/criterion/tarski_gate_v1); an unregistered criterion resolves N[missing_binding].

Tarski-gate self-reference detector for JudgedExpr claims. Returns B[self_reference] when any symbol argument inside the judged inner expression names the enclosing claim's own id (the claim judges itself); otherwise returns T. Deterministic.
Semiclassical GR evaluator. Predicate leaves by NAME; DynamicExpr claims by SUBJECT symbol (declared unboundedness is assertable). Unknown names/subjects resolve N[undefined_term].
Executable adequacy method: recomputes 0.99, agreeing with the attested score (the runtime uses the attested score directly when present).

Registered adequacy method that declares its score not yet computable (returns the non-numeric sentinel "N"). The runtime pins the assessment as N[not_yet_applicable] (spec sections 9.2/16.6.4: score N from a RESOLVED method is deferral, not a binding gap) and emits a warning diagnostic adequacy_score_not_yet_applicable — the not-yet-ness IS the verdict (quantum-gravity core description is open).

Degrade-mode bridge carrier for the semiclassical-to-core extrapolation. The runtime's builtin execute_transport implements degrade internally (spec section 10.2 default degradation: T -> N[transport_loss], support partial); the via URI is carried in provenance and registered in the live pack as a marker only.
Unitary-dynamics evaluator for the decoherence-cat panel.
Collapse-postulate evaluator for the decoherence-cat panel.
Degrade-mode micro-to-macro amplification bridge losing phase_coherence. Builtin degrade semantics apply (T -> N[transport_loss], support partial); via URI registered as a marker.
ZFC-frame evaluator: the duplication theorem holds (duplicable(sphere)=T) and contradicts naive volume preservation (volume_preserved(sphere)=F).

ZF-frame evaluator (no axiom of choice), REGISTERED in the live pack but deterministically undecided on choice-dependent predicates: duplicable and volume_preserved resolve N[missing_binding] (no binding without AC). Unknown predicate names resolve N[undefined_term].
Executable adequacy method: recomputes 0.98, agreeing with the attested score.

cases.name: Live conjunction over mixed atoms
normalized_ast_expectations: t, f, b, n in expression position -> zero-arity PredicateExprNode
c1..c4 -> LogicalExprNode; truths computed LIVE by the spec section 4 pair algebra over atoms_v2 leaf results, not echoed from claim-id-keyed expectations
expected values from the spec section 4 tables: B AND N = F (flagship), T AND B = B, T AND N = N, F OR N = N

composed B/N results carry the section 16.6.6 derived reason: the unique reason of the determining sub-results (the ones sharing the composed truth) is inherited — c2 inherits source_conflict from b, c3 and c4 inherit undefined_term from n. Composed T/F results carry no reason (c1 = F; F reasons are optional annotations per section 8.5).

cases.name: Live disjunction and negation
normalized_ast_expectations: c1 -> LogicalExprNode(op=or); c2, c3 -> LogicalExprNode(op=not) with a single argument
expected values from the spec section 4 tables: B OR N = T, NOT B = B, NOT N = N (negation swaps the pair bits; B and N are fixed points)
section 16.6.6 reason derivation: c2 (NOT b -> B) inherits source_conflict and c3 (NOT n -> N) inherits undefined_term from their single determining operand; c1 (B OR N = T) carries no reason
block fold over live results T, B, N hits the B-and-N-present rule: block(local) = F

cases.name: Derived connectives with canonical spellings
normalized_ast_expectations: the canonical EBNF operator spellings are pinned in source: "->" (ImplOp) -> LogicalExprNode(op=implies); "<=>" (IffOp) -> LogicalExprNode(op=iff)
expected values from the spec section 4 derivations: B -> N = (NOT B) OR N = B OR N = T; B <=> N = (B -> N) AND (N -> B) = T AND T = T

cases.name: Unparenthesized operator precedence
normalized_ast_expectations: EBNF A.9 binding tightest-to-loosest is NOT > AND > OR > IMPLIES > IFF; the first-match split order is loosest-first, so OR splits before AND
c1 -> or(and(t, f), t); computes OR(AND(T,F),T) = OR(F,T) = T. Pins the tree shape; the inverted tree and(t, or(f, t)) happens to compute T as well, so c2/c3 carry the truth-level discrimination
c2 -> or(and(f, t), t) = OR(F,T) = T; the inverted-precedence tree and(f, or(t, t)) would compute F, so a precedence regression is detectable by truth alone
c3 -> or(n, and(t, b)) = OR(N,B) = T; the inverted-precedence tree and(or(n, t), b) would compute B, a second truth-level discriminator that also exercises the pair algebra on B/N atoms

cases.name: Non-associative operator chains (left-associative)
normalized_ast_expectations: 3-operand IMPLIES/IFF chains normalize to LEFT-NESTED BINARY LogicalExprNodes per the EBNF iteration order (`IffExpr ::= ImplExpr { IffOp ImplExpr }` line 1235, `ImplExpr ::= OrExpr { ImplOp OrExpr }` line 1236, reconstructed spec A.9): c1 -> iff(iff(t, f), f); c2 -> implies(implies(f, t), f); c3 -> implies(implies(t, b), n). Never a flat 3-ary node (see the ast_decision "IMPLIES/IFF chains are left-associative binary trees"; m7 red-team CRITICAL-1).

c1: t <=> f <=> f = iff(iff(T, F), F) = iff(F, F) = T. The red-team discriminator: BOTH associativity readings give T, while the truncating evaluator (dropping operands past the second) computed iff(T, F) = F — so the pinned T proves no operand is dropped.

c2: f -> t -> f = implies(implies(F, T), F) = implies(T, F) = F. Pins the LEFT-associative reading specifically: right association would give implies(F, implies(T, F)) = implies(F, F) = T, and truncation would give implies(F, T) = T — only left association yields F.

c3: t -> b -> n = implies(implies(T, B), N) = implies(B, N) = (NOT B) OR N = B OR N = T (pair algebra: implies(T, B) = F OR B = B). Truncation gave B — a second dropped-operand discriminator exercising B/N atoms; the composed T carries no reason.
block(local) folds the live results T, F, T -> F

No runtime lint-13 diagnostic exists; lint rules live in the analyzer, not the conformance runtime.

cases.name: Schwarzschild singularity forensics

c2 -> DynamicExprNode(op=approaches, subject=curvature): the sketched |inf:finite_time| target is not legal surface syntax (baseline refs are fixed at offset 0), so declared unboundedness is pinned as the symbol target divergence_within_finite_time, evaluated T by the live dynamic-expression handler

The vendored ast_decision unresolved_method -> N[missing_binding] still governs methods with NO registered handler (see ast_decisions; m7 red-team MEDIUM-1 remediation).
